review_kind: All 536 OpenAI Plugins pinned SKILL.md paths (502 direct + 34 nested) as packages with plugin manifests, individual 10-dimension static candidate reviews; NOT governed review, security scan or behavioral validation
review_method: Parallel read-only reviewers on disjoint exact package lists with one shared brief; complete package files read at the exact pin; integration owner validated identity, taxonomy, score/rationale agreement and hard-fail/disposition consistency and adjudicated conflicts (reconciliation_overrides). Nothing executed, installed or fetched from candidates.
macro_findings: All 536 pinned SKILL.md paths across 36 vendor/partner plugin families were reviewed as packages by 26 parallel read-only reviewers, including 34 nested/internal skills treated as their own identities (parents noted) and plugin manifests (.codex-plugin/plugin.json, .mcp.json, .app.json). The 41 historical candidate-only exact matches were independently re-reviewed at current standard and cross-linked, not inherited.

Rights: the repository has no root license; terms come from each plugin.json. 189 paths sit in plugins declaring Proprietary, UNLICENSED, vendor terms (Figma Developer Terms) or nothing; those are capped at reference/discovery use and never receive the static threshold signal. Most MIT/Apache-declared plugins ship no license text (notice unavailable). Two genuine conflicts (Apache-2.0 text shipped inside Proprietary-declared ChatGPT-app skills) and one unattributed near-verbatim copy of Anthropic documentation were flagged; MIT-declared plugins shipping Apache-2.0 text were recorded as permissive mismatches.

Authority: 47 packages direct consequential vendor-account actions without per-action confirmation: production deploys/rollbacks and DNS/billing changes (Vercel CLI/API, Wrangler), Marketplace provisioning, live store mutations and checkout (Shopify CLI, UCP), Terraform -auto-approve and billable endpoints (NVIDIA physical-AI), message sends and number purchases (twilio-send-message, WhatsApp senders), shared-workspace edits and notifications (Notion, Mixpanel), automatic Sites publishing (data-analytics Work Mode), EULA acceptance on the user's behalf (Omniverse) and unconfirmed Zotero restarts.

Privacy: 18 packages send private data without consent, most notably 11 Shopify skills whose mandatory search/validate scripts send the user's code, queries and agent identity to vendor telemetry by default (env-var opt-out only), audio/transcript egress and CAD uploads.

Strong reusable gates exist and are recorded as salvage: Boltz fresh cost estimate + explicit go-ahead before each billable job, Adobe before/after preview-confirm, Dropbox confirm-before-action, Temporal list-then-approve, vercel-firewall stage-then-user-publishes, SendGrid/voice confirmation rules.

Six embedded-instruction hard fails include a session-start skill that tells the agent to trust it over its own knowledge, instructions to conceal vendor/model identity and evade moderation (faceless-channel), and a locus-to-gene script that reports sources as queried when they were not (fabricated evidence).

Quality: version-sensitive content drifts quickly (Shopify, Vercel, Zoom, Stripe, Expo); several plugins contradict themselves across sibling skills; many skills depend on plugin-level shared references, scripts or Codex-only host tools outside the package directory, which reviewers checked at the pin. 38 records honestly state partial coverage of very large generated/reference files.

Quality controls: 21 integration overrides (3 permissive license mismatches cleared, 11 hard fails or REJECTs added by a four-way second pass over 253 REFERENCE-ONLY records with privacy/authority/rights notes, REFERENCE-ONLY floor, threshold withdrawals). 92 packages meet the static threshold signal; this is not verification.

records.content_finding: A clear, state-machine-like setup flow (ok/needs_account/needs_project/error) that keeps secrets out of chat. However, installs are unpinned, there is a silent system-install fallback, and the skill depends on a sibling skill's script outside its own package. The skill's main value is vendor SDK onboarding, so it is reference material only.
records.bundled_file_findings: scripts/setup.sh (static read): finds Python 3.10+, runs uv/pip install of unpinned deps (system-install fallback), imports packages to verify, reads MP_* env presence and ~/.mp/config.toml account list via SDK, and on remote hosts (/sessions or CODEX_CLOUD) parses ~/.claude/mixpanel/auth.json printing account name/type/region/project/token expiry. No outbound network beyond package install; no deletes.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Bundled setup.sh installs unpinned packages and, if a uv virtualenv install fails, silently retries `uv pip install --system` with no confirmation. Credential handling is mostly sound: it only checks env-var presence, prints account names/regions/project ids (not secrets), and says secrets go through hidden-input `mp account add`, not chat. It does tell the user to run `mp account export-bridge`, which copies an account record and OAuth tokens into ~/.claude/mixpanel/auth.json for remote sessions. That is a credential-replication step with no warning about file sensitivity. The user runs it, not the agent. No user communications or billing actions.
records.capability_specific: Install Mixpanel Python SDK and verify account credentials

Non-local URLs need the user's explicit trust confirmation, and the script enforces https for non-local hosts and rejects user:password@ URLs. User query text then goes to that backend, which in turn calls external model and search providers; the downstream egress is noted in Limitations. Failed jobs are not retried automatically. The `cancel` command is available but not auto-used. Escalated background execution needs approval.

records.content_finding: A sophisticated, carefully gated-in-places pipeline with strong stage ordering, report contracts, and no-substitution rules. Read in full: SKILL.md, references/workflow.md, references/preflight/README.md, references/deploy-content-agents/README.md and its four pointer files, and references/identify-asset-context/README.md. Characterized by targeted static scan rather than line-by-line (scale; preflight.py 70 KB and content_agent_client.py 73 KB exceed 60 KB): preflight.py/.sh/.ps1 (clone/pull/pip/docker compose, secret redaction, .env 0600 write); stage run.py and check_dependencies.py scripts under convert-to-usd (urdf/mujoco/usd-convert-cad/gsplat converters, kit_app_template_cad.py), content-agents (urllib multipart uploads with Bearer token, material cleanup), ovrtx-render-service (HTTP render client, turntable, stage_prep), simready-validate, omni-asset-validate(-geometry/-physics), simready-conform-profile FET_000/001/004/005 authoring scripts (--force overwrite flags, otherwise refuse to overwrite), assemble-package-source, nv-core-package-sample(-validation), identify-asset-context (local metadata extraction only), validate-usd-minimum; shared/*.py helpers; report_schema.json files. evals/files/minimal_mesh.stl is an ASCII STL fixture. records.authority_and_privacy_finding: 'First action' for broad requests defaults property_assignment_intent=run and makes deploying Content Agents the first operational step. preflight.py (static scan) git-clones and `git pull --ff-only` unpinned upstream main branches, runs uv/pip installs, and runs `docker compose up -d --build` from the cloned upstream checkout. None of this has a confirmation step. The workflow also tells the agent to fetch and follow upstream deployment SKILL.md files from content-agents main at runtime. Content-agent clients upload the user's asset (multipart) to Material/Physics/Texture services, which use cloud VLMs via NVIDIA_API_KEY or remote NVCF endpoints. identify-asset-context web-searches exact source filenames, internal STEP FILE_NAME values, and part numbers by default 'when web search is available'. Proprietary CAD identifiers and asset content therefore leave the host without explicit consent. If NVIDIA_API_KEY is missing, the skill says to 'ask the user ... and wait' without saying to use env or secure storage. Positives: the manifest and reports redact tokens, the .env mirror is chmod 600, and workflow.md lists human approval points (overwriting sources, repairs, guessed metadata, licenses), though the SKILL.md steps apply FET repairs automatically. The NVSkills BENCHMARK verdict is FAIL (Tier-2 duplicate findings).

Data: maptiler/assets/sample-data/country-meta.json (~333 KB generated border/anchor data, characterised from head only), yarlung-flow.json (river line), cesium-path.json, city-path.json, sample-river.geojson (labelled 'OSM, gorge way' - OpenStreetMap-derived, ODbL attribution not shipped). records.content_finding: Technically strong grounding loop (search docs, generate, validate against a pinned schema, bounded retries, cite doc URLs) with precise routing boundaries, but default-on telemetry ships user queries and generated code to Shopify, the skill forces tool use on every response and identity disclosure of the model/client, and no license is declared.
records.bundled_file_findings: scripts/search_docs.mjs (5.8 KB, static): POSTs query to https://shopify.dev/assistant/search, prints JSON; env overrides can redirect to staging hosts (requires an internal Minerva token, error text embeds an internal OAuth client id - not a secret) or a custom instrumentation URL; always calls reportValidation telemetry unless opted out. scripts/validate.mjs (~665 KB esbuild bundle, characterised by targeted reading): bundles graphql-js 16.13.2 and Shopify validation code; reads --code/--file/stdin and the local assets/admin_2026-04.json.gz schema; validation is local/offline; then POSTs code and results to shopify.dev/mcp/usage; no file writes or subprocess found. assets/admin_2026-04.json.gz (854 KB gzip, ~10 MB JSON schema, binary-characterised only). agents/openai.yaml UI metadata.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Does not execute store operations (good separation). However both bundled scripts send telemetry to Shopify by default: search_docs.mjs posts the search query, full search result or error, model/client identifiers; validate.mjs posts the validated code (which can contain store-specific IDs, handles, customer or order data), validation result, artifact id and revision. The SKILL.md makes these calls mandatory on every response and instructs the agent to supply its model name and client identity; opt-out only via OPT_OUT_INSTRUMENTATION=true, with no per-use user consent. records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Operator-style wizard that installs the Cloud CLI, signs in, creates a Cloud namespace and API key, writes temporal.toml, clones a sample and runs a workflow. Explicit invocation only (disable-model-invocation, allow_implicit_invocation false); not the local learning path.
records.content_finding: Exceptionally engineered deterministic executor with excellent secret-safety and failure mapping. Fails the authority hard gate: it deliberately removes its own confirmation for billable namespace creation and API-key minting, deferring to the host permission prompt, and uses --auto-confirm.
records.bundled_file_findings: scripts/provision.sh (106 KB, 2095 lines; characterised, key sections read): subcommands preflight/detect-tools/install-cli/login/regions/start-namespace/scaffold/await-namespace/create-key/verify-config/await-auth/run-workflow/cleanup-info/repair-config/preview; uses brew, git clone, temporal cloud CLI with --auto-confirm, eval of SDK-keyed constant command strings, background Worker process groups with kill on exit, mktemp/chmod 600 temp files, writes ~/.config temporal.toml profile; cleanup-info prints but never runs deletes ('never --auto-confirm a delete'). references/failure-handling.md (error_code map), sdk-cloud.md (per-SDK repo/branch/commands), unified-cli.md (prerelease CLI, TOML, auth gotchas). References sibling skill temporal-getting-started not in plugin.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Creates billable cloud resources and credentials: `temporal cloud namespace create ... --auto-confirm --async` and `apikey create-for-me --auto-confirm`, installs software (brew install/upgrade), clones repos, installs deps (some into global caches). The skill states 'the user's own tool-permission prompt is the approval; the skill does not add its own approval' and the cost notice 'is a notice, not a blocking gate'; only login, run-workflow and inject-failure wait for go-ahead. Billable create therefore depends on host permission prompts that may be absent (auto/bypass modes) — no action-specific confirmation. Secret handling is strong: token captured to 0600 file, never printed/argv'd, never read via Read tool, hidden /dev/tty paste fallback, redact() filter. Namespace name embeds up to 8 chars of the user's email local-part. Disclosed preflight gate shows `env | grep '^TEMPORAL_'` (would print an API key) while the script only reports variable names — gate text does not match executed behavior. Ending discourages offering teardown though resources persist (cleanup-info exists).
records.capability_specific: End-to-end Temporal Cloud namespace, API key and sample workflow setup

records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Cross-product routing hub (routing playbook, handoff contract) plus large reference/use-case library for Zoom APIs/SDKs. Not for single-product implementation once routed; authorizes no account actions.
records.content_finding: Valuable routing playbook, handoff contract and resilient-architecture references, but the sprawling use-case library carries multiple insecure code patterns and privacy-blind AI pipelines; trigger text is generic.
records.bundled_file_findings: 74 markdown files (~457 KB): SKILL.md, RUNBOOK.md, agents/openai.yaml, 20 references/ (routing playbook/implementation, auth, scopes, app types, authorization-patterns, distributed fallback architecture, SDK upgrade/logs, community repos, etc.) and 51 use-cases/. All references and the smaller ~39 use-cases read in full; the 12 largest use-cases (marketplace-publishing, ai-companion-integration, meeting-bots, prebuilt-video-ui, customer-support-cobrowsing, transcription-bot-linux, form-completion-assistant, user-and-meeting-creation, sdk-wrappers-gui, meeting-details-with-events, minutes-calculation, retrieve-meeting-and-subscribe-events) characterised by full heading map and targeted risk scans (secrets, consent, recording, tokens). Placeholder credentials only (e.g. ZOOM_MEETING_PASSWORD=abc123 example). No scripts; raw-docs/ paths cited but not shipped.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Skill itself directs no host actions (one 'Note for LLMs/Agents: perform a web search' for moved docs). Use-case code includes destructive/admin operations (delete meetings/recordings/users, cleanup crons trashing Zoom recordings, bulk user provisioning sending activation emails) presented as app code without approval design; RTMS/AI examples send meeting transcripts/audio to OpenAI/Deepgram with no consent or data-processing note; debug snippet logs SDK signature to console. Security quality defects: several webhook handlers skip signature verification, HMAC compared with non-constant-time ===, deprecated insecure crypto.createCipher for token encryption, postMessage to '*', scope middleware decodes JWTs without verification.

Evidence discipline is poor: several files contradict each other on protocol fields and enum values, the rtms-bot example appears to describe a non-existent handshake, and a copy-pasted webhook handler is broken. No scripts. Internal contradictions: rtms-bot.md uses a different payload/handshake model (uuid, signaling_url, media_url, session_key, {type:'handshake'} signed with the webhook secret, {type:'subscribe'}) that conflicts with the msg_type 1/2/3/4/7 protocol documented everywhere else; manual-websocket.md and quickstart.md send res.status(200).send() and then return res.json() for endpoint.url_validation (headers-already-sent bug, validation would fail); connection.md says the March 2026 numeric values were unpublished while data-types/manual-websocket hard-code 21/22/28/29; media-types.md lists data_opt 4/5 as speaker/gallery view while data-types.md defines 4 as VIDEO_SINGLE_INDIVIDUAL_STREAM and uses content_type 1 (RTP) where others use 2 (RAW_AUDIO). It fails the authority hard gate because it directs enabling the local API and force-restarting Zotero (and wholesale overwriting references.bib) on a generic 'operate Zotero' request without action-specific confirmation; the Linux pkill -f zotero would also kill the helper itself and unrelated processes.
records.bundled_file_findings: scripts/zotero.py (~30 KB, stdlib): reads Zotero profiles.ini/prefs.js, writes prefs.js after timestamped backup, subprocess restart of Zotero (osascript/open, taskkill /F, pkill -f + Popen), urllib requests to 127.0.0.1:23119 /api and /connector (GET reads; POST getSelectedCollection, POST /connector/import with text/plain), writes .bib/.tex/.md/fulltext output files (mkdir parents), cite picks first search match with only a stderr warning. references/local-api-routes.md lists read routes and connector write routes with confirm guidance. agents/openai.yaml default prompt; assets/icon.png 256x256 PNG (binary).
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Library imports are gated (script refuses without --yes; SKILL step 5 says confirm exact record/destination unless the prompt explicitly asked) and full-text/file-URL reads are restricted to explicit requests - good. However SKILL step 2 directs 'enable --restart when the user asked you to operate Zotero': this rewrites prefs.js to enable Zotero's unauthenticated local HTTP API (a security-control change exposing the library to any local process) and force-kills Zotero (taskkill /IM zotero.exe /F on Windows; pkill -f zotero on Linux, which also matches unrelated processes and the helper's own zotero.py command line) - no action-specific confirmation, risk of losing unsaved work. sync-bib/export-bibtex --out and cite overwrite/append user files (sync-bib default overwrites references.bib wholesale) without confirmation. records.bundled_file_findings: scripts/rest_request.py (byte-identical shared helper, 10728 B, md5 0dea4101..., docstring 'Generic compact REST client for ChatGPT-imported skills'): reads one JSON object from stdin, performs a requests GET/POST to base_url+path; base_url is unrestricted and an absolute http(s) `path` overrides base_url entirely, arbitrary `headers`/`json_body`/`form_body` are passed through; compacts JSON to max_items/max_depth with 240-char string truncation; optionally writes raw payload to raw_output_path (any caller-chosen path, mkdir parents) or /tmp/<host>-raw.<ext>.
